radio.ble: Bluetooth Low Energy via nRF52832 / S132

open_field_range.guidance: There is no fixed LoRa maximum range. Range depends on antenna gain/height, spreading factor, bandwidth, TX power, receiver sensitivity, Fresnel clearance, interference and regulatory limits.
open_field_range.ideal_conditions_note: Distances above 10 km can be possible with appropriate antennas and clear line of sight, but are not a product guarantee without a field link-budget test.

electrical.recommended_note: Do not connect a source that can exceed 3.6 V directly to the board supply.
electrical.lipo_3v8: A 3.8 V nominal LiPo is not suitable for direct connection because it is already above the 3.6 V board limit and can reach about 4.2 V when fully charged. Use a low-quiescent-current regulator/buck-boost sized for radio current peaks.

features: persistent VM program and persistent user state
external 32.768 kHz crystal and nRF52 DCDC profile
NinaLink low-power LoRa Node / BLE-NDP Bridge transport for Home Assistant
Persistent 16-bit NinaLink Network ID isolation and automatic node discovery
Optional 256-bit Application/NDP owner key for Home Assistant access
Remote NinaLink capability controls and behavioral commands through the bridge
advantages: BLE and LoRa on the same compact board
Programmable behavior through nRFclaw VM without reflashing application firmware
Sensor/event-oriented execution allows peripherals to remain off when not needed
Home Assistant/NDP integration plus physical NUS programming path
NinaLink nodes keep Application/NDP off and duty-cycle LoRa contact windows for battery operation
Home Assistant can use either Direct BLE or a NinaLink Bridge without changing node application semantics
limitations: Supply must remain between 2.5 V and 3.6 V
LoRa range is installation-dependent and cannot be guaranteed from frequency/SF alone
Continuous LoRa RX consumes far more power than event-driven/sleep operation
BLE advertising interval directly affects average current
Some pins are reserved by onboard peripherals and cannot be treated as free GPIO simultaneously
HALFMOON has a known shared physical pin between LoRa DIO2 and DS18; NINASENSE Rev1.1 does not use that same mapping
A NinaLink Bridge keeps LoRa RX active continuously and therefore is a higher-power gateway role than a NinaLink Node
The NinaLink Network ID isolates networks but is not a substitute for the optional Application/NDP owner key

cr2032.note: Actual usable capacity depends strongly on cell brand, temperature, pulse current, cutoff voltage and aging.

tracking_2s.note: Uses the measured 2 s BLE advertising current as an engineering proxy; validate the exact tracking payload/current on the production board before giving a guaranteed lifetime.

semantic_defaults.machine_anomaly_event: Natural machine/vibration anomaly wording maps to VIB_AUTO.ALARM when no other anomaly detector is named.
semantic_defaults.lora_alert_payload_note: If a behavior asks only to send an alert over LoRa and supplies no payload text, the deterministic standalone lowerer uses VIB_ALERT and reports this default as a warning.
semantic_defaults.lora_unspecified_profile: Uses the current host compiler LLCC68 defaults unless frequency/power/SF/BW/CR are explicitly supplied.
semantic_defaults.machine_on_event: Natural wording that a machine starts/begins running maps to VIB_AUTO.MACHINE_ON and HA app operation 1.
semantic_defaults.machine_off_event: Natural wording that a machine stops/finishes running maps to VIB_AUTO.MACHINE_OFF and HA app operation 5.
semantic_defaults.machine_warning_event: Natural wording that vibration becomes unusual/strange maps to VIB_AUTO.WARNING and HA app operation 3.
semantic_defaults.machine_alarm_event: Natural wording that vibration becomes abnormal/anomalous maps to VIB_AUTO.ALARM and HA app operation 4.
semantic_defaults.telegram_via_ha: Telegram wording means the device emits the corresponding Home Assistant event; Telegram delivery is performed by Home Assistant, not by the nRF52832.
semantic_defaults.hall_volume: A prompt such as Every HALL1 pulse represents 1 liter accumulates a persistent total in compiler-owned state[15] and publishes retained semantic VOLUME to Home Assistant.

DIRECT_BLE.transport: BLE advertisements plus short Application/NDP sessions
DIRECT_BLE.power: low-power role; passive telemetry/events are advertisement-driven where possible

NINALINK_NODE.transport: duty-cycled NinaLink LoRa contacts through a separate bridge
NINALINK_NODE.power: battery-oriented; LLCC68 and MCU return to the low-power path between contact windows

BRIDGE.transport: continuous NinaLink LoRa RX plus BLE/NDP to Home Assistant
BRIDGE.power: higher-power gateway role because LoRa RX remains active

ndp_owner_key.note: Once configured, Application/NDP access requires this key. Physical P0.21/NUS remains the owner/recovery path.

network_id.purpose: network isolation/admission; this is not the NDP authentication key

ninalink.bridge_prompt: Enable Home Assistant in bridge mode.
ninalink.node_prompt: Enable Home Assistant in LoRa mode on network 0x1234.
ninalink.node_reuse_prompt: Enable Home Assistant in LoRa mode.
ninalink.provisioning: For prompt --upload, the bridge reuses or creates a non-zero Network ID. A first-time node must be given the bridge Network ID. Host provisioning occurs before bytecode upload.
ninalink.low_power_rule: Node role disables Application/NDP and duty-cycles LoRa. Bridge role keeps LoRa RX continuous and is not a low-power-node role.
